Split diagram showing the morphology of a forage grass and a forage legume. Left side: A grass plant (like Guinea grass) showing fibrous roots, a cylindrical jointed culm with visible nodes and internodes, a leaf sheath wrapping the stem, a parallel-veined leaf blade, and a branching panicle inflorescence at the top. Right side: A trailing legume (like Centrosema) showing a deep taproot with small round root nodules, a trailing stem, compound leaves with three broad net-veined leaflets, and a small bean-like pod. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background, clear distinct labels for every part mentioned.

Split diagram contrasting Hay and Silage making. Left side (Hay): A sunny, open field with cut grass lying on the ground, and a tractor using a baler machine to produce rectangular bales of dry, brownish hay. Right side (Silage): A cross-section of an underground pit silo. The pit is lined with a thick plastic sheet, filled to the top with closely packed, chopped green forage, tightly covered over the top with more plastic, and weighed down heavily by a layer of soil and old tires to keep out all air. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.
